clue.text: Engineers longing for repair job?

definitions.note: a gerund, the act of putting right, read as a noun

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
longing for something is dying for it, as in dying for a drink

explanation.surface: Army mechanics yearn to be sent out on a fix-it task.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineers here are the British Army's repair corps, which makes the surface neatly self-referential; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something right is mending it, so the act of mending is a repair job.

clue.text: Eurovision hit Verdi composed in state of ecstasy? Not initially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the shortened word
the first letter of the word for the ecstatic state is dropped

parts.note: a trance is a rapt, ecstatic state

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Verdi piece arranged for Eurovision sends viewers into raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' turns VERDI into IVERD, which goes 'in' RANCE (TRANCE with its first letter removed by 'Not initially').
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish dance show began as the interval act at the 1994 Eurovision Song Contest and became a huge hit.

clue.text: Sailor displaying Jolly Roger at first

parts.note: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is used here

explanation.surface: A seaman flies the pirate flag, the skull and crossbones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly Roger' looks like the pirate flag; split it, and Jolly is a marine while 'at first' takes R from Roger.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who sails ships for a living.

clue.text: See 1
Safe place for money, as it turns out

indicators.note: out signals the words are put out of order, rearranged into a new phrase

explanation.surface: Somebody discovers the best spot to keep their cash after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IT TURNS; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Money held in trust is kept safely by trustees on someone's behalf, so the phrase describes a secure place for it.

clue.text: Detailed how maul got out of control in one part of the pitch

indicators.note: out of control says the letters run wild into a new order
read as de-tailed: the first word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A rugby report describes a scrum getting messy in one area of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' trims HOW to HO; 'out of control' then rearranges HO, MAUL and GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The area right in front of a goal on a football or hockey field is part of the playing surface.

clue.text: It's a really big bra size that would take me aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the size is read from end to start

parts.note: a K cup is an extremely large bra size

explanation.surface: A huge bra size would take the speaker by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take me aback' sounds like surprise, but 'aback' turns KCUP round and 'me' is the setter, whose pseudonym this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter signs this puzzle with this pseudonym, so the first person refers to that name.

clue.text: Clear as daylight, two sides to tennis court grievances

parts.note: something clear as daylight is plain and obvious

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tennis players' complaints about the court are perfectly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a tennis court, but goes with the definition: legal complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a plaint is a written statement of a complaint brought before a court.

clue.text: Narrow escape when visiting the neighbours?

definitions.text: Narrow escape when visiting the neighbours?

parts.words: Narrow escape when visiting the neighbours?
parts.note: a near miss, and also a social visit paid to people living nearby, read as a call that is close

explanation.surface: Popping round next door turns out to be a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave or near miss is an escape by a small margin, the idiomatic meaning.

clue.text: Our tiny vehicle originally transported exotic seed

indicators.note: transported means carried away, so the letters are moved into a new arrangement
originally points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A small car has carried some foreign seeds across the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges OUR TINY with V, the first letter of 'vehicle' picked by 'originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard seed of a South American palm, used as vegetable ivory for buttons, is a tropical seed.

clue.text: Flower seller online

definitions.meaning: a river, something that flows, here the great South American one
a huge internet retailer of books and much else

explanation.definitionFit: The great South American river shares its name with the giant internet retailer.

clue.text: House of Tudor angered some

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A member of the Tudor royal family has upset a few people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House of Tudor' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'House'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch royal dynasty is the House of Orange, and William of Orange took the English throne.

clue.text: In Paris a motorboat started by girl departs without a crew

parts.note: the French for the article a is un

indicators.note: started by refers to the opening letter of the word

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: In Paris a girl sets off a motorboat and leaves it to sail without anyone aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanned means having no staff or people aboard to operate it.

clue.text: Second car is an old one

definitions.note: one refers back to car: a vintage British make

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
RR is short for Rolls-Royce
taken as written

explanation.surface: A second-hand car turns out to be a vintage model.
explanation.walkthrough: MORRIS was a British car maker whose Morris Minor is a classic; 'one' refers back to 'car'.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris is a defunct British marque, so a Morris is an example of an old car.

clue.text: Deliberately stirred purée briefly with spoon

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters are shuffled together
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Somebody intentionally mixes purée with a spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts PUREE to PURE, and 'stirred' rearranges PURE and SPOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something deliberately is doing it intentionally, by design rather than accident.

clue.text: A day in dopey stupor, endlessly like t-h-i-s?

indicators.note: the card and day go inside the muddled letters
dopey means befuddled, so the letters are muddled
endlessly removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: an ace is the card marked A

explanation.surface: Someone spends a day in a drugged haze, endlessly stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STUPOR to STUPO, 'dopey' rearranges that to SPOUT, and ACE and D go 'in'. 'A' as ace is a playing-card convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters with hyphens between them are set apart from one another, graphically illustrating the phrase.

clue.text: Regular occurrence after marshalling yard shut

indicators.note: marshalling means arranging into order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Railway trucks routinely get shunted once the marshalling yard closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marshalling yard' reads as one railway phrase; 'marshalling' is the anagram indicator, with YARD SHUT the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week comes round every seven days, so it happens regularly.

clue.text: Southern friends touring part of London with extra on-board fare

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the friends surround the district

parts.note: pals are friends
EC1 is a London postcode district, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Southern rail pals on a London trip enjoy extra food on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: EC1 is a postal district of central London; the digit 1 is treated as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Special meals ordered for a flight are known as specials, extras to the standard food.

clue.text: Change name in secret

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for secret

parts.note: covert means secret

explanation.surface: Someone alters their identity in a clandestine way.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to transform it into another form, a synonym of altering.

clue.text: Setter leaves South American country with something family will share

indicators.note: leaves means departs from, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Suriname is a country on the north coast of South America
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler leaves a South American country with something shared by relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' as I is a crossword convention: the compiler speaks in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name is passed down and held in common by members of a household.

clue.text: Sleuth managed to put pressure on

indicators.note: managed means handled or manipulated, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A detective succeeded in leaning on a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To hustle someone is to push or pressurise them into acting, a synonym of coercing.

clue.text: Wind is up before doctor leaves the country

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top
leaves means goes out of, so those letters come out of the country's name

parts.note: Morocco is a North African country
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A wind picks up as the physician flees the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses IS to SI, and 'leaves' takes MO out of MOROCCO to leave ROCCO.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa into southern Europe has this name.

clue.text: King with a French way about his pretentious magnificence?

parts.note: GR is George Rex, King George
and means with or plus

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the French word is reversed

parts.note: rue is the French for street

explanation.surface: A monarch with French manners puts on a show of pompous splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses RUE to EUR; 'a' and 'his' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour or impressive grandness, which may be put on for show.

clue.text: Fry-up I concocted, free from anything unsavoury

indicators.note: concocted means cooked up, so the letters are mixed afresh

explanation.surface: A healthy cook rustles up a cleaner version of a full English breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: A fry-up is a British cooked breakfast of fried bacon, eggs and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse something is to rid it of contaminants or impurities, as the definition describes.

clue.text: Penny and the others put back what's moved during earthquake

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so the shorthand is reversed

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and the others

explanation.surface: Penny and her companions restore something that moved during a tremor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses ETAL to LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthquakes happen when sections of the Earth's crust slip against each other.

clue.text: Cast finally look into naming group leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A theatre director finally examines who is named in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like an instruction to take a last letter, but it is one of the words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something is to hurl it, as you cast a stone or a line.

clue.text: Wife's left hat with old jacket

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: a bowler is a hard round felt hat
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife has left behind a hat and an old coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes W out of BOWLER to leave BOLER, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket, originally Spanish, worn above the waist.

clue.text: Lawless one meeting end in electric chair, perhaps

parts.note: an means one, a single thing

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters
end in takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An outlaw meets his end in the electric chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges C (the last letter of 'electric') with CHAIR into ARCHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means without order or rule, so a state or person behaving that way is lawless.

clue.text: Two thirds fly back for exam

indicators.note: back means the shortened insect is read in reverse
two thirds of a six-letter word keeps four letters, dropping the last two

parts.note: the tsetse is an African biting fly

explanation.surface: Two thirds of an insect flies back for an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two thirds' cuts TSETSE to TSET, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination of knowledge or ability.

clue.text: Characteristic air with which Esme casually wears skimpy garment

indicators.note: wears says the rearranged name goes inside the garment, which is worn around it

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy undergarment

indicators.note: casually means in a relaxed, haphazard way, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A tune plays while Esme casually puts on revealing underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' rearranges the name, and 'wears' puts the result inside the garment; 'with which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune associated with a show, person or film is its signature tune.
